subject: english
question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

If you permit me, / I will bring and show / all my drawings to you.
solution:
The correct answer is Option(1) i.e.** "No error​"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence structure is correct as is, with no grammatical errors present.
 
• The sentence is a **first Conditional Sentence. [If + Subject + verb(base form) ,+ Subject + will/shall + **verb(base form)]
 
• The phrasal construction allows for both actions **"bring"** and** "show" **to be directed towards **"all my drawings to you"**, maintaining clarity and cohesiveness in communication.

Therefore, the correct sentence is- ***"If you permit me, I will bring and show all my drawings to you."***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"I will bring and show" **is not incorrect because it denotes two actions that the speaker intends to perform, both of which are grammatically and contextually appropriate.
 
• **"If you permit me," **sets up a conditional clause properly and does not contain any grammatical errors.
 
• **"all my drawings to you" **despite being potentially debated for its positioning, functions well within the sentence and is understood to be grammatically fitting once reviewing for contextual sense and readability.
